text.p: Here are highlights of stories in Romania's press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
Business:
ROMANIA LIBERA
- Tens of thousands of hectares of arable land in the Braila county damaged by floods.
- Labour Minister Alexandru Athansiu quoted as saying government social protection scheme to help population cover up to 75 percent of expected price rises.
ADEVARUL
- Prices for medicines expected to rise this month.
- Farmers affected by new fuel prices, the paper says.
LIBERTATEA
- Consumer goods prices expected to rise by 30 percent following recent fuel price hikes.
CURIERUL NATIONAL
- Traffic on River Danube hampered by floating ice.
General:
ROMANIA LIBERA
- The government is expected to discuss on Monday social protection measures to compensate price hikes following a recent decision to double petrol prices.
- The increase in petrol prices was triggered by the former leftist government's failure to take such steps ahead of last year'sd elections, a government statement said.
EVENIMENTUL ZILEI

- Romanian ambassadors to France, Germany, Britain and Austria were recalled soon after the new foreign minister was appointed. The country's ambassador to the U.S., Mircea Geoana, is still in office.

- Leftist opposition Party of Social Democracy (PDSR) slammed the government for failing to stick to electoral promises by doubling petrol prices. It said the measures will trigger hyper-inflation and economic collapse.
- Romanian state television to appoint its leading board on Monday and change heads of main departments.
LIBERTATEA
- Prime Minister Victor Ciorbea is expected to submit this week a report on his 200 days as Bucharest mayor.
ADEVARUL
- Former Romanian President Ion Iliescu to become leader of the PDSR.
- White House National Security Adviser and Defence Undersecretary Walter Slocombe is expected to make visit to Romania to discuss costs of country's NATO integration.
ZIUA
- Romania and Bulgaria might get special financial support from the G7 countries due to their delays in economic reforms, newspaper says quoting private ProTV television.
JURNALUL NATIONAL
- Bucharest pigeons are hunted for food, the newspaper says quoting the A.M. Press local news agency.
($= 4,136 lei) -- Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
